cells.tense: You are choosing this direction right now, and your hands are steady.
cells.ask: Name one person or commitment you are carrying, and say out loud the direction you have chosen to move in with them.
cells.core:
You have chosen the direction and you are carrying it without forcing. It feels like the plainest thing in the world, not a load you are bracing under. Two streams have joined and you are moving with them, not against the pull of your own caution. You know which direction you chose, and you are glad to carry it.

Your strength is doing its work and it stays soft enough to listen. That is what balance looks like here. Say the direction out loud — not for anyone's approval, just so the choice sits in the room where people can meet you in it. You are already moving; this just lets them see where.
cells.sheetLine: You are holding steady and moving with the current you chose.
cells.verb: Choosing the current that carries you both
cells.place: The place where you keep standing under what has not lifted

cells.tense: You are already gripping a future that has not arrived yet, and your hands are tired.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are holding for someone else and put it down for a day, without explaining why.
cells.core:
You are carrying weight that has not been handed to you yet. You can feel the needs of people who have not asked, the outcome of a conversation you have not had, and your body is braced for a load that may not come. That bracing is what is spending the strength you have.

Carrying has turned into clutching. The flow you want is not more effort. It is letting the current carry what you have been trying to carry by yourself. Set one thing down today. You do not have to announce it. Just see whether it stays afloat without your hands on it.
cells.sheetLine: You are bracing for a weight that is not yours to hold yet.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you, and your feet have not moved.
cells.ask: Tell one person something true about what you are carrying, and let them hear it without asking them to fix it.
cells.core:
You are staying out of the room and calling that endurance. The weight is on you and you are not letting anyone stand near it. Your strength has not gone, but it is not moving with anything right now. It is just standing where it was told to stand.

The way back is not feeling more or pushing harder — that would only tax what is already thin. It is letting one person know what you are carrying, exactly as it is, with no request attached. That is how the current finds you: not by you reaching for it, but by you showing up where it runs.
cells.sheetLine: You went still to keep carrying, and the weight has no one in it.
cells.verb: Choosing the current that carries you both
cells.place: The place where you keep standing under what has not lifted

cells.tense: You are already holding the line for both of you, and you are calling it just what has to be done.
cells.ask: Say out loud that one thing you are keeping steady for someone else is yours to hold, and let that be true for a moment.
cells.core:
You are keeping something stable that other people lean on, and you do not count it as yours. You would say you are just practical, just getting through, just doing what has to be done. But what people feel from you is real, and it shapes how they move, whether or not you claim it.

Your hands are doing work in the room, and the one person giving it no credit is you. Name one thing you are keeping stable and say that it is yours. Not vanity. Just the plain fact of what you are already doing, said in your own voice.
cells.sheetLine: You are already the steady one. You just have not said so.
